question: Wipro Elite NTH (Project Engineer) technical interview. **Compare C and Java: syntax, features and applications.** The candidate was also asked to **rate themselves in C and in Java** and justify the ratings. Related questions in the same interviews covered pointers, functions, variables, classes, objects, inheritance, interfaces and polymorphism.
lookingFor: Accurate, structured comparison rather than a random list.
Understanding of compilation and execution models, memory management and platform independence.
Honest self-assessment backed by concrete experience.
answer:
**Core idea.** C is a procedural, low-level language compiled directly to machine code. Java is an object-oriented language compiled to bytecode that runs on the JVM.

| Aspect | C | Java |
|---|---|---|
| Paradigm | Procedural | Object-oriented (class-based) |
| Execution | Compiled to native code per platform | Bytecode, run by JVM (write once, run anywhere), with JIT |
| Memory | Manual: `malloc`/`free`; pointers and pointer arithmetic | Automatic garbage collection; references, no pointer arithmetic |
| Safety | Buffer overflows and dangling pointers possible | Bounds-checked arrays, exceptions, stronger type safety |
| Features | Structs, macros, preprocessor, `goto` | Classes, inheritance, interfaces, exceptions, generics, threads, large standard library |
| Inheritance | None | Single class inheritance, multiple interface implementation |
| Syntax | Functions are standalone; `main` returns int | Everything inside classes; `public static void main` |

**Applications.** C: operating systems, embedded systems, drivers, compilers, performance-critical code. Java: enterprise back ends, Android apps (historically), web services, large business systems.

**Syntax notes.** Both use similar braces, loops and operators, which is why the syntax looks close. Java has no header files and no pointers; strings are objects (`String`) while in C they are null-terminated `char` arrays.

**Rating yourself.** Give a number and a reason, for example "7/10 in C: I understand pointers, arrays, structures and dynamic memory and I wrote programs with them, but I have not worked on systems-level code. 6/10 in Java: I use classes, collections and exceptions in my project but I am still learning concurrency." Avoid 10/10 and avoid very low scores; both invite hard follow-ups.

**Mistakes to avoid:** saying Java is "slower, so worse" without context, or claiming Java has no pointers at all (it has references).
followUps: What is the difference between a pointer in C and a reference in Java?
Is Java platform independent? Is the JVM?
Why does Java not support multiple inheritance of classes?
Write a simple program in your stronger language to reverse a string.
